source_caption:
For Terminator 2: Judgment Day, Arnold Schwarzenegger was paid around $15 million, which was a massive salary at the time. What makes it even more interesting is how little he actually speaks in the film. With roughly 700 words of dialogue, it comes out to about $20,000+ per word, turning lines like “Hasta la vista, baby” into some of the most expensive in movie history.

But that paycheck wasn’t just for dialogue. Schwarzenegger spent months training with weapons, learning tactical movements, and working on physical precision to make the Terminator feel believable and machine-like. Director James Cameron also pushed for minimal dialogue on purpose, wanting the character to come across as cold, efficient, and almost mechanical.

The film itself was one of the most expensive ever made at the time, with a budget of around $100 million, largely due to its groundbreaking visual effects, especially the liquid metal T-1000. It paid off—Terminator 2 became a huge box office success and is still considered one of the greatest action and sci-fi films ever. Schwarzenegger’s performance, despite the limited lines, became iconic, proving that screen presence can matter more than how much a character actually says.
